newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures end mixed, yen holds gains.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures end mixed, yen holds gains.

text.p: IMM currency futures ended mixed, with yen and marks holding slim gains in an uneventful session, traders said.

They said floor trade was active in the Canadian dollar and Mexican peso pits where total open interest for both contracts rose to a record 78,591 and 30,194, respectively, during Wednesday's pit session.
"Pesos were very volatile today," one floor trader said, adding that about 2,000 contracts traded in the exchange's all-or-nothing pit. The all-or-none pit accepts orders of 100 lots or more.
Several firms, both large and small, were buyers throughout the day, while a Japanese firm and German bank, as well as several U.S. houses, were active sellers, traders said.

They said there was decent activity in Canadian dollar futures, but trade was less than the purchase of 4,500 June contracts and the purchase of nearly 5,100 exchange-for-physical (EFPs) Canadian dollar contracts on Wednesday. EFPs, which are not transacted in the pit, allow a customer to buy or sell cash commodities for a short or long futures positions.
December Canadian dollars fell to $0.7448, below Wednesday's low at $0.7442, but are expected to resume their rally in the near term, traders and analysts said.
"The Canadian dollar is rallying out of a 10-year head-and-shoulders position," one floor trader said. "We are looking for December to rise to $0.7526."
The intermediate-term upward target of $0.7526 is equivalent to 1.3327 spot. Longer-term, he is looking for the lead Canadian dollar contract to climb to $0.8000, or 1.2541 spot.
Like Canadian dollar futures, sterling also succumbed to profit-taking, but traders are no less bullish on the pound.
"Technically this market is telling you that any selling should be met with buying," one trader said. He attributed declines to the sterling's performance against the cash mark.
December yen were slightly higher, as the contract continued to find support off the contract low of $0.008906. December nearly re-tested that level on GLOBEX.
"Once we get through exporter sell-orders at the 113.00/05 area, the dollar/yen will really shoot higher, one trader said. The 113.00 level corresponds to December's contract low.

At the end of pit trade, December yen was up $0.000006 at $0.008920, marks rose $0.0006 at $0.6601, Swiss francs fell $0.0026 at $0.7998, sterling lost $0.0040 at $1.5924, Canadian dollars were down $0.0010 at $0.7456, Australian dollars were down $0.0013 at $0.7910, and pesos were $0.000300 lower at $0.122450. -Derivatives desk 312-408-8750;E-mail derivatives@reuters.com
